title: Viniyoga of the arghya

words.meaning: of the mantra of the giving of the arghya
gāyatrī, the metre of three lines of eight syllables
in the giving of the arghya

words.role: what the mantra is used for

samasa.meaning: the mantra of the giving of the arghya

translation.literal: Of the mantra of the giving of the arghya: Viśvāmitra the seer, divine gāyatrī the metre; Savitṛ the deity, the use in the giving of the arghya.
translation.readable: The arghya mantra (the Gāyatrī): seer Viśvāmitra, metre gāyatrī, deity Savitṛ; used for offering the arghya.

meaning: A viniyoga is the statement said before a mantra of its seer (ṛṣi), its metre (chandas), its deity (devatā) and the use (viniyoga) it is put to. Here: the Gāyatrī, tat savitur vareṇyam (TS 1.5.6.4; RV 3.62.10), used for the arghya, the water offered to the Sun. Viśvāmitra is its seer and Savitṛ its deity. The commas of the witness mark the pauses between the parts; a word before a comma keeps its pausal form.
in_the_rite: Step arghya, after the saṅkalpa for the arghya and before the vyāhṛtis and the Gāyatrī, in all three services (M only).
